---
name: request-missing-record
description: Draft a narrow California public-record request for an identified planning, water, grant, GIS, or permit record that is not publicly retrievable.
---

# Request a missing record

1. Name the custodian that created or maintains the record.
2. Identify the project, system, agreement, permit, case number, date range, and
   known document IDs.
3. Request existing native electronic records and attachments, including
   metadata and redlines where they exist. Do not ask the agency to create an
   analysis.
4. Include applications, staff reviews, final instruments, amendments,
   exhibits, correspondence, and transmittals only when relevant.
5. For GIS, request native vector data, layer metadata, coordinate system, and
   map project files—not only a PDF.
6. For permits, request the application, technical or engineering report,
   approved plans, permit, amendments, inspection correspondence, and conditions.
7. Ask for rolling production and identification of withheld records and the
   specific exemption asserted.
8. Record the request, date, custodian, scope, response deadline, productions,
   and unresolved items in the case corpus.

Keep requests narrow enough that an agency can search them without guessing.
Public accessibility of an index does not prove that the underlying file was
produced or reviewed.
